description: Expected relate outcomes for the identifier-keyed fixture — join keys spelled with raw registry names, never renamed to *_id. Each entry names the candidate edge (child.column -> parent.column), the status relate must assign it, and the status it got BEFORE edges were scored on finetype's types. `accepted_edges` is the complete accepted set: any edge not listed there must not auto-accept.

expected_edges.why: a checksum-valid identifier column against a unique parent, discovered with no rename; scored 0.44 when key-likeness came only from spelling, and untyped it is accepted only through the exact-name key credit, because its values are key-shaped
the second directional key of the same link table, same reason
the names share no substring, so name similarity is 0.0 and the candidate never reached scoring; shared identifier typing is what gets it past the prune

every accept gate passes — 0 orphans, unique parent, confidence over the line — but the child types as LEI and the parent as ISIN, so the edge is demoted for review rather than accepted; it stays in the descriptor carrying both types; untyped there is no mismatch to demote on, and the exact-name key credit accepts it
